overview.title: Indian Press Act 1910
overview.definition: A draconian legislative measure enacted by the British Government of India to curb the rising tide of nationalist sentiment and revolutionary activities by empowering local authorities to demand security deposits from printing presses and newspapers.
overview.importanceInUpsc: It represents the peak of colonial censorship, illustrating the shift from 'regulation' to 'suppression' of the Indian nationalist press, frequently appearing in questions regarding the evolution of civil liberties and colonial administrative policy.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Indian Press Act 1910.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Context**: Enacted in the backdrop of the **Swadeshi Movement** and the rise of **revolutionary terrorism** (Anushilan Samiti, Yugantar).
• **Mechanism**: Empowered the **Local Government** to demand a security deposit (ranging from Rs 500 to Rs 2000) from any printing press or newspaper publisher.
• **Forfeiture**: If the press published 'objectionable material' (defined broadly to include anything inciting hatred against the government), the security could be forfeited and the press seized.
• **Appellate Authority**: The Act provided for an appeal to a **Special Tribunal of the High Court**, but the burden of proof rested heavily on the publisher.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Subjective interpretation used to silence dissent

items.definition: The primary executive authority empowered to demand security without prior judicial intervention.
A three-judge bench of the High Court; the only legal recourse, though rarely ruled in favor of the press.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Targeting**: Specifically aimed at vernacular newspapers and radical journals like 'Yugantar' and 'Sandhya'.
• **Impact**: Led to the closure of hundreds of presses and the forfeiture of massive sums of money.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Total erosion of freedom of expression; stifling of political discourse.
• **Solutions**: Repealed in 1922 based on the recommendations of the **Tej Bahadur Sapru Committee**.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-A-F-E' (Security, Appeal, Forfeiture, Executive).
• **Decoded Meaning**: S-Security deposit required; A-Appeal to High Court; F-Forfeiture of press; E-Executive power supreme.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 1910 Act with the 1878 Vernacular Press Act. Remember: 1910 Act applied to ALL presses (English and Vernacular), whereas 1878 was specifically for Vernacular.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Legislative Repression' to describe the 1910 Act in the context of the 'Constitutional vs. Revolutionary' struggle.

keyTakeaways: The 1910 Act was a revival of the worst features of the 1878 Vernacular Press Act.
It effectively silenced the radical press during the peak of the revolutionary movement.
The Act was finally repealed in 1922 following the recommendations of the Press Laws Committee.
